page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a fixed 3.3 GHz clock frequency using the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor design. The CPU topology features a 1:1 core-to-thread allocation without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, delivering a 2:1 ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with no onboard GPUs, and the instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 17 Gbps. Architectural flags indicate hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions, while traditional x86 vector extensions and nested virtualization features are not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional integer, compression, and compilation execution. The system achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core (2,382.0), multi-core (25,987.0), and Clang compilation tests (63,901.0). Single-threaded data handling is notably efficient, shown by top-decile scores in gzip compression (36.46 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.26 GB/sec). Memory subsystem tests recorded strong small-block cached read throughput of 4,319.78 GB/sec and a top-tier PassMark database operations metric of 47,005.39. Web serving capacity reached 92.57 GB/sec, alongside strong Redis performance at 93.19 million operations per second.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARMv9 core allocation provides predictable multi-core throughput and high power-performance density without virtualization jitter from hyperthreading. The configuration is primarily matched to compute-bound batch jobs, software compilation pipelines, microservices, in-memory caching fleets, and high-throughput web serving architectures that do not require dense local disks or dedicated GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized ARM64 virtual server powered by 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz on the AWS Neoverse-V3 ARMv9 architecture. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 17 Gbps baseline network throughput, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks confirm top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core (2,382.0) and multi-core (25,987.0) compute, Clang software builds, and data compression workloads such as gzip (36.46 GB/sec). It also demonstrates top-decile throughput in web serving and PassMark database operations. With dedicated core execution and consistent memory bandwidth, c9g.8xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, distributed containerized microservices, high-traffic web tiers, and compute-focused data transformation tasks.
